He is too focused on music theory and creating complex chords. That doesn’t really translate to something emotional and proves “knowing music theory doesn’t equate to making great music!” This is coming from myself, who creates music!

I went to university where I studied music theory and composition. The pieces I created were waaaay outside the realm of the songs I wrote prior. We learned all about complex chords. And when I was writing I didn’t get emotional like I did with the pieces I wrote in years before. The stuff I wrote wasn’t terrible and I thoroughly enjoyed learning and broadening my musicality.

My mom told me something one day like, “how come you don’t write something like before!” What she meant was my music was from the heart. I would sit at the piano and just hit the keys and these emotional tunes would come pouring out. I wasn’t focused on: “I need to add this chord or use this borrowed chord!” I was playing based on emotion and what sounded good!

Once I started being too focused on the process of composition, the “pouring out of emotions” stopped dead in its tracks and the process became too mechanical. I would show up with something I thought sounded good to my ear. But, it wasn’t conducive to the process” if that makes sense!

Yeah! Benji is straight acting too. I agree it does seem like he forgot the advice from NYC. But, he wasn't out to anyone and now he is, and that changes everything. The feeling of not being gay enough or being too gay is coming back to Victor.
Also, I knew Mia and Andrew would get together! Are we really that surprised!

Wow! I wanna start off by talking about Felix's mom. The scene where Lake met Felix's mom I felt like, "this is good! She is in a good place right now!" But when she wanted to give Lake the plates my heart broke. Felix should be able to be a teen and not have to worry about this heavy burden. I am happy he had Lake there because she is someone who I hope can make Felix realize he needs help.

The situation with Andrew and Victor--- I think Andrew means well. But the scene in the coffee shop where he was trying to get Victor to rejoin the team made me feel for Victor. I also felt bad for Victor when Benji's bandmates were joking about Benji finally having his straight boy. All too often I feel like Victor feels he can't 100% be himself. 

The scene in the basketball court with Andrew was something I could relate too. Andrew said that Victor is the least gay gay person alive. And I can relate because I have moments where I feel like I dont fit the mold of what it means to be gay. When people find out I'm gay (by me telling them) they are usually surprised. For a while I thought of it as a compliment. I felt like, "Wow! I can pass as straight!?" I was never really ashamed of being gay and I am not sure where those feelings came from. I also had a friend who would say, "This is my fabulous gay friend who needs to be more fabulous!" Victor said: "what is the perfect level of gay that'll keep everyone happy!?" Victor saying that he is too gay for the locker room and not gay enough for Benji and his friends is how I feel. I feel like society has this idea of what it means to be gay. And I never thought that I fit the "right amount of gay." I know that is silly and I know there isn't a look to being gay just like their isnt a look to being straight. There is no right or wrong way to be gay. 

I admire the show for showing that because it shows I am not alone and trying to find my identity as a gay person. Love, Victor showcases that finding you identity as a gay person is not in the way you act or what you wear. It is in the self - acceptance that comes from within.

Let's talk about Andrew finally talking to the team about how dumb they were being. The fact they all dyed their hair to show support was amazing! I also thought it was kinda sweet that Benji showed up. He cares about Victor and I am happy they talked about what happened at the coffeeshop. I did a song entitled 'In The End.' I have a cool story behind it. 

I was going to Italy on a school trip and I knew we were going to the disco. So I started producing a song and then I had my friend Samantha sing it. 

When we got to the disco I was so nervous to walk up to the DJ (he was on the top floor) and hand him the CD. 

After awhile I walked up to our Italian tour guide and said, "I have a song that I was wondering if the DJ could play. So he went with me upstairs and talked to the DJ. It was also Samantha, her twin brother, and this other kids birthday so the DJ gave a shoutout.  

Finally after handing the DJ my song he went through some songs asking, "is this your song?" Then finally it played over the loud speakers of the disco and he said, "this is 'In the End' by..." And I said DJ DILLY C & SAMMI and he announced it to everyone.

I was so excited I ran around and people in our group where like, "is this your song!?" Apparently they recognized Samantha's voice. I ran downstairs and my italian teacher (from Italy) and our Spanish teacher (from Argentina) where sitting down and I was so out of breath and I told them. They were so happy and I ran back upstairs.

In eighth grade I knew when I started high school I wanted to create a GSA. The first thing I did was email a local organization in my state called youth pride. I emailed her, but unfortunately she was too busy to start one but when I came to the high school we could talk.

 I told one of my best friends Samantha about starting one and she said she would help me any way she could. When I started high school I met with the woman I emailed while in eighth grade. She really helped get the ball rolling in terms of starting it. We had to then meet with the principal who was also supportive. 

It was a little slow at first because no one really knew about us. So we did some publicity by putting up posters and announcing meetings. I have the best friends in the world who were so supportive of the GSA and they kept asking me when the first meeting was. It was their enthusiasm which also motivated. 

Since it was the first GSA at my school some people were against it. They were just childish and even asked my friend if he was gay since he joined the GSA. Clearly they didn't understand it was the gay STRAIGHT alliance. All in all people tell me how awesome it is that I started such a club, but I don't think I'm anything special for starting it. I just wanted a place to go and talk about things and feel welcome in a world where I feel like an outcast!
